nodes.summary: For distinct points `a ≠ b` of a finite type, exactly a `1 / |β|` fraction of the functions `h : α → β` satisfy `h a = h b`: `|{h | h a = h b}| · |β| = |α → β|`.
nodes.title: Collision count of a uniformly random function

nodes.summary: The random-hash protocol for equality costs at most `k + 1` bits.
nodes.title: Cost of the random-hash protocol

nodes.summary: It is at most the cost of the public-coin protocol.
nodes.title: Cost of the induced randomized protocol

nodes.summary: Every deterministic protocol run by a public-coin protocol has depth at most its cost.
nodes.title: Each run costs at most the cost

nodes.summary: `disjFn n x y` is `true` iff the subsets of `{1, …, n}` with characteristic vectors `x` and `y` intersect; this is the function `DISₙ` of N. Alon, Y. Matias and M. Szegedy, J. Comput. System Sci. 58 (1999), Section 3 (its negation is set disjointness).
nodes.title: Set intersection function

nodes.summary: Against any input distribution `μ`, some deterministic protocol in the support of an optimal randomized protocol has `μ`-error at most `ε` (the easy direction of A. Rao and A. Yehudayoff, *Communication Complexity*, early draft, Theorem 3.3).
nodes.title: Distributional complexity is at most randomized complexity

nodes.summary: `distComplexity f μ ε` is the least depth of a deterministic protocol whose error under the input distribution `μ` is at most `ε` (A. Rao and A. Yehudayoff, *Communication Complexity*, early draft, Chapter 3, "average-case" error; fixing the random string, a randomized protocol does no better against a fixed distribution). For `ε ≥ 0` such a protocol exists; otherwise the value is `0` by the convention `sInf ∅ = 0`.
nodes.title: Distributional communication complexity

nodes.summary: For a distribution `μ` on input pairs, the probability under `μ` that `p` answers wrongly for `f`.
nodes.title: Distributional error of a deterministic protocol

nodes.summary: With shared random function `h : {0,1}^n → {0,1}^k`, Alice sends the `k` bits of `h x` and Bob announces whether they equal `h y` (A. Rao and A. Yehudayoff, *Communication Complexity*, early draft, Chapter 3, Figure 3.1).
nodes.title: Random-hash protocol for equality

nodes.summary: `1` if the protocol `p` answers wrongly on `(x, y)` for the function `f`, and `0` if it answers correctly.
nodes.title: Error indicator of a protocol

nodes.summary: On distinct inputs the random-hash protocol errs with probability exactly `1 / 2 ^ k`: it errs exactly when the random function collides on `x` and `y` (A. Rao and A. Yehudayoff, *Communication Complexity*, early draft, Chapter 3: "if `x ≠ y`, the probability that `h(x) = h(y)` is at most `2^-k`").
nodes.title: Error of the random-hash protocol for equality

nodes.summary: The random-hash protocol never errs when `x = y`.
nodes.title: No error on equal inputs

nodes.summary: For `f : X → Y → Bool` and an input pair `(x, y)`, the fraction of random strings `r : R` on which `run r` outputs a value other than `f x y`.
nodes.title: Error probability of a public-coin protocol

nodes.summary: The error of a public-coin protocol, as a fraction of random strings, is the error of the randomized protocol it defines.
nodes.title: The two notions of error agree

nodes.summary: With shared random function `h`, the protocol outputs `true` exactly when `h x = h y`.
nodes.title: Output of the random-hash protocol

nodes.summary: There is a constant `C₀` such that for every `n ≥ 1` and `0 < ε ≤ 1 / 2`: if `g : {0,1}^n × {0,1}^n → {0,1}` is computed by a public-coin protocol (with a nonempty finite set of random strings) of cost `c` and error at most `ε` on every input, then it is computed by a private-coin protocol, with nonempty finite sets of private random strings, of cost at most `c + log₂(n / ε²) + C₀` and error at most `2ε` on every…
nodes.title: Newman's theorem

nodes.summary: For a deterministic protocol `p` in which Alice holds `(x, a)` and Bob holds `(y, b)`, the fraction of pairs `(a, b) ∈ RA × RB` of private random strings on which `p` outputs a value other than `f x y`.
nodes.title: Error probability of a private-coin protocol

nodes.summary: The largest depth of the deterministic protocols it runs, over all random strings.
nodes.title: Cost of a public-coin protocol

nodes.summary: A family `run r` of deterministic protocols indexed by the shared random string `r : R`; the string is drawn uniformly from the finite set `R`, independently of the inputs (A. Rao and A. Yehudayoff, *Communication Complexity*, early draft, Chapter 3).
nodes.title: Public-coin randomized protocol

nodes.summary: For every fixed $0 \le \varepsilon < 1/2$ there is $c > 0$ such that, for every $n$, every public-coin protocol that decides whether two subsets of $\{1, \dots, n\}$ intersect, with error at most $\varepsilon$ on every input, has worst-case cost at least $cn$: $R_\varepsilon(\mathrm{DIS}_n) \ge cn$.
nodes.title: Randomized communication complexity of disjointness

nodes.summary: For every `n` and `k`, equality of `n`-bit strings has randomized communication complexity at most `k + 1` with error `2 ^ (-k)`, by the random-hash protocol (A. Rao and A. Yehudayoff, *Communication Complexity*, early draft, Chapter 3, Figure 3.1); deterministically it needs `n + 1` bits for `n ≥ 1` (`commComplexity_eqFn`).
nodes.title: Randomized communication complexity of equality

nodes.summary: For finite input sets and `ε ≥ 0`, the randomized communication complexity of `f` with error at most `ε` on every input equals the largest, over distributions `μ` on input pairs, of the least depth of a deterministic protocol with error at most `ε` under `μ` (A. Rao and A. Yehudayoff, *Communication Complexity*, early draft, Theorem 3.3, proved there from von Neumann's minimax theorem).
nodes.title: Yao's minimax principle for communication complexity

nodes.summary: `randComplexity f ε` is the least cost of a randomized protocol whose error on every input pair is at most `ε` (A. Rao and A. Yehudayoff, *Communication Complexity*, early draft, Chapter 3, "worst-case" error). For finite inputs and `ε ≥ 0` such a protocol exists. If none meets the bound (for instance when `ε < 0`, or possibly for infinite inputs), the value is `0` by the convention `sInf ∅ = 0`.
nodes.title: Randomized communication complexity

nodes.summary: The largest depth of a deterministic protocol in its support.
nodes.title: Cost of a randomized protocol

nodes.summary: The probability that the drawn protocol answers wrongly for `f` on the input pair `(x, y)`.
nodes.title: Error of a randomized protocol

nodes.summary: A finitely supported probability distribution on deterministic protocols: the protocol actually run is drawn from it, independently of the inputs, and both parties see the draw (A. Rao and A. Yehudayoff, *Communication Complexity*, early draft, Chapter 3: "a randomized protocol can be thought of as a distribution on deterministic protocols").
nodes.title: Randomized protocol

nodes.summary: The uniform distribution on the random strings, pushed forward along `run`.
nodes.title: A public-coin protocol as a randomized protocol

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
